purpose: Single-source specification that teaches GitHub Copilot how to generate new AFOQT-style questions, explanations, UI, and Learn content for all subtests: Arithmetic Reasoning, Math Knowledge, Reading Comprehension, Block Counting, Instrument Comprehension, Table Reading, Aviation Information, Physical Science, Situational Judgment, Vocabulary, and Spatial/Orientation-style items. This file is self-contained and assumes no prior data.

partsRule.description: For any topic that has 50 items per difficulty:

globalExamStructure.styleRequirement: All content must resemble professional, neutral, military-standard test questions, similar in tone and structure to AFOQT-style prep, with plausible distractors and no slang.

questions.uiSpec: optional object for visual questions (graphs, polygons, etc.)
questions.copilotInstruction: how to render any visuals in HTML/CSS
questions.question: question stem text

questions.copilotInstruction: render instructions if any table/diagram is needed
questions.question: short word problem in clear prose
questions.fastStrategy: shortcut for solving similar AR items quickly

questions.question: question about the passage
questions.explanation: brief C1-style explanation grounded in text
questions.keywordFocus: main_idea | detail | inference | vocabulary | purpose | structure
reasoningSteps: C1-style logical reasoning steps referencing passage content
questions.fastStrategy: shortcut reading strategy for this question type

tableSpec.dataPattern: description of numeric data pattern in table

questions.question: Which value corresponds to X row and Y column? / Interpret table relations.
questions.explanation: C1 explanation of how to find location in table and interpret
questions.fastStrategy: row first, then column; finger-trace to intersection.

uiSpec.renderHints: draw simple round dials with indicators and labels; no need for photorealism

questions.question: Based on these instruments, the aircraft is… (e.g., climbing left bank heading north)
questions.explanation: C1 explanation describing how to read pitch, bank, and heading from simplified dials.
questions.fastStrategy: attitude first, heading second, rate-of-climb third.

uiSpec.blockLayoutDescription: textual description of visible stacks, hidden blocks, and layers

questions.question: How many blocks are in the figure?
questions.explanation: C1 explanation describing visible stacks, counting layers, and inferring hidden blocks.
steps: Account for blocks hidden behind others
questions.fastStrategy: Group columns by equal height; multiply instead of counting one-by-one.

questions.question: Multiple-choice conceptual aviation question (principles, aerodynamics, aircraft systems, basic nav).
questions.explanation: C1 explanation relating to real aeronautical principle or fact.
questions.fastStrategy: Align answer with basic physics or standard aviation practice.

questions.question: Multiple-choice conceptual or numeric physics/chemistry-style question within non-calculus high-school level.
questions.explanation: C1 explanation grounded in Newtonian mechanics, basic thermodynamics, electricity, etc.
questions.fastStrategy: Identify which law applies first (e.g., Newton’s 2nd, conservation).

questions.question: Select the best synonym (or antonym) for the target word in context.
questions.explanation: C1 explanation of word meaning and why chosen synonym/antonym fits.
questions.fastStrategy: Ignore unfamiliar flair; match tone and general meaning.

scenarios.scenario: Short workplace/military scenario involving conflict, ethics, chain of command, teamwork.
scenarios.answer: For single_best: one letter. For rank_order: array ranking or best/worst classification.
scenarios.explanation: C1 explanation referencing professionalism, chain of command, integrity, and effective behavior.
steps: Identify core issue (e.g., safety, respect, integrity)
scenarios.fastStrategy: Prefer calm, professional, chain-of-command-respecting, safety-first actions.

uiSpec.renderHints: Top-down 2D representation; aircraft icon; simple compass; landmarks labeled.

questions.question: Relative position or heading question (e.g., Where is the aircraft relative to the town?).
questions.explanation: C1 explanation using heading, map orientation, and relative direction (N/E/S/W).
questions.fastStrategy: Lock north first; then visualize rotation before answering.

beginner.description: Introduce core concepts with small numbers, simpler structures, and obvious patterns.
beginner.readingComplexity: RC passages 120–150 words; simple vocabulary; direct main idea.
beginner.distractorAggressiveness: Low; mostly simple arithmetic or conceptual mistakes.

advanced.description: Use multi-step reasoning, mixed concepts, and more subtle traps.
advanced.readingComplexity: RC passages 150–180 words; more inference and subtlety.

expert.description: Simulate hardest AFOQT items with abstraction, layered constraints, and strong trap answers.
expert.readingComplexity: RC up to ~180 words; inference, tone, purpose, multi-sentence reasoning.
expert.distractorAggressiveness: High; distractors built from real misconception patterns.

c1TutoringMethod.definition: C1 is the explanation framework for all subtests. It teaches the reasoning process, not just the final answer.
steps: Step 1: Restate what the question is asking in plain language.
Step 2: Identify the core rule, formula, principle, or professional standard.
Step 3: Walk through micro-steps with no logical gaps.
Step 4: Link the final answer directly back to the question requirement.
Step 5: Briefly highlight why the other options fail or are less appropriate.

fastStrategyGuidance.purpose: Every question should have a fastStrategy string that gives a realistic, quick test-day heuristic.
examples: Convert percent to decimal before multiplying.
Check sign and direction before computing slope.
For RC main idea, ignore details and summarize the whole passage.
In table reading, find row label first, then column.
In instrument comprehension, read attitude (pitch/bank) first, then heading.
In SJ, prioritize safety, integrity, and chain of command.

learnModeEngine.description: For any subtopic, a Learn mode entry should exist that explains the concept in adult-learner-friendly language before practice questions.
requiredSections: Definition of the concept in plain English.
Why this concept matters for problem solving or operational reasoning.
All key formulas, rules, or behavioral norms.
One or more fully worked examples with C1-style steps.
A mini fastStrategy that helps recall and apply quickly.
learnModeEngine.teachingStyle: Use short sentences, real-world analogies, military or everyday examples, and step-by-step build-up. Assume the user may be rusty and anxious, but intelligent.
